story.fullStory:
Des'ree's "You Gotta Be" reached #5 on the Billboard Hot 100. "You Gotta Be" is an R&B/soul song by British singer and songwriter Des'ree, written by her with Ashley Ingram, who produced the song.

It is the third track on the singer's second album, I Ain't Movin' (1994), and the opening track on the US release of that album.

The song was released as a single in March 1994 by Sony Soho Square, becoming a top-40 hit in several countries, and a top-10 hit in the United States and Australia.

The song peaked at #5 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 44 weeks on the chart.

facts.text: "You Gotta Be" is an R&B/soul song by British singer and songwriter Des'ree, written by her with Ashley Ingram, who produced the song.
It is the third track on the singer's second album, I Ain't Movin' (1994), and the opening track on the US release of that album.
The song was released as a single in March 1994 by Sony Soho Square, becoming a top-40 hit in several countries, and a top-10 hit in the United States and Australia.
The song peaked at #5 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 44 weeks on the chart.
I Ain't Movin' is the second studio album by British soul singer-songwriter Des'ree.
It was released on 9 May 1994 in the UK, and 5 July 1994 in the US by 550 Music and Epic Records, and features the top 5 smash hit, "You Gotta Be".
In the US, "Feel So High" was featured on and released as a single from I Ain't Movin' rather than from Des'ree's debut album Mind Adventures.

Desirée Annette Weekes (born 30 November 1968), known by her stage name Des'ree (), is a British pop and soul recording artist and songwriter, who rose to prominence during the 1990s.
You Gotta Be was released in 1994.
The song appears on the album "I Ain't Movin'" (1994).

Known for her distinctive contralto voice and uplifting lyrics, Des'ree's biggest hits include the singles "Feel So High", "You Gotta Be", and "Life", as well as the ballad "Kissing You", which featured on the soundtrack of the 1996 film Romeo + Juliet.
She was named Best British Female at the 1999 Brit Awards.
